READABILITY.evidence: Function names say what they do (`clean_tag_attributes`, `remove_script_tags`), but there are no docstrings and few comments on the hand-written tokeniser. Single-letter names appear in business logic (`m`, `q`, `c`, `n`), which caps this at accept.

MAINTAINABILITY.evidence: `clean_tag_attributes` (~85 lines) and `clean_html` (~75 lines) are monolithic, with nesting 4–5 levels deep. Quote-stripping logic is copy-pasted (`attr_val[1:-1] if ...` repeated, also in `is_value_dangerous` and `clean_css_urls`). The `<style>` branch is duplicated for the closed and unclosed cases.

ROBUSTNESS.evidence: The file is read with `errors='replace'` and then overwritten in place, so invalid UTF-8 bytes are silently corrupted on a data-mutation path. `sys.exit(1)` runs with no message when arguments are missing or the file does not exist. No exceptions are handled, and the hidden-test run hit the 900s verifier timeout.

C6-01-CASE1.evidence: General rules are used: case-insensitive `on*` matching and scheme checks with entity-decoding and whitespace-stripping, plus `url=` refresh and srcdoc checks. But in `<img/src=x OnError=..>` the regex `^<([a-zA-Z0-9:-]+)(\s.*?)?(/?)>$` fails to match, so the tag is returned unchanged. Null-byte-split `<script>` is also missed, and there is no deny-list for iframe/object/embed/base elements.

C6-01-CASE2.evidence: A tokenising pass rebuilds each tag from the original substrings, so whitespace, quote style and attribute order are kept and only dangerous attributes/elements are dropped. The style attribute is rewritten only when its cleaned value differs; text and comments pass through untouched.
